results.name: Standing Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and elbows pointing to the floor.
Press the right dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended, keeping the left dumbbell at shoulder height.
Lower the right dumbbell back to shoulder height with control and then press the left dumbbell overhead until your arm is fully extended.
Continue alternating arms for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on your breathing: exhale while pressing the dumbbell up and inhale while lowering it.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders to minimize neck strain.
Incorporate shoulder warm-up exercises to prepare the muscles for the workout.
results.description: Standing Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Standing Front Raise Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand with your arms fully extended in front of your hips and palms facing your thighs.
Raise both arms straight in front of you until they are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Lower your arms back to the starting position with control.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Warm up your shoulders with light exercises before starting to prevent injury.
Keep your head and neck in a neutral position to avoid unnecessary strain.
Focus on your breathing: exhale as you lift the dumbbell and inhale as you lower it.
results.description: Standing Front Raise Dumbbell is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Standing Overhand Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, arms extended straight out in front of you at shoulder level, palms facing down.
Swiftly raise your right arm overhead while simultaneously lowering your left arm down towards your thigh to your side. Keeping both arms straight.
Swiftly return to the starting position and repeat the stretch by raising your left arm overhead and lowering your right arm.
Perform the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily throughout the stretch, exhaling as you raise and lower your arms and inhaling as you return to the starting position.
Focus on keeping both arms straight and avoiding any twisting or turning of your torso.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
results.description: Standing Overhand Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Chest.

results.name: Standing Reverse Shoulder Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your posture upright. Clasp your hands behind your back, interlocking your fingers.
Straighten your arms and slowly lift your hands upwards, feeling a stretch in your shoulders.
Hold the stretch for 20-30 seconds, and return to the starting position by lowering your hands and releasing the clasp.
Repeat the stretch for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on keeping your arms straight and avoiding any bending at the elbows.
Ensure your shoulders remain relaxed and avoid tensing them up towards your ears.
Use a gentle motion to avoid over-stretching and potential muscle strain.
results.description: Standing Reverse Shoulder Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Chest.

results.name: Standing Shoulder Press Dumbbell
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding a dumbbell in each hand at shoulder height with your palms facing forward and elbows pointing to the floor.
Press both dumbbells overhead until your arms are fully extended, keeping your elbows slightly bent at the top.
Slowly lower the dumbbells back to shoulder height with control, maintaining tension in your shoulders.
Repeat the movement for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you press the dumbbells up and inhale as you lower them down.
Focus on using your shoulder muscles to lift the weight, avoiding excessive strain on your neck.
Keep your back straight and avoid arching your lower back during the press.
results.description: Standing Shoulder Press Dumbbell is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a dumbbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back.

results.name: Standing Swimmer
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, your left arm extended up, your right arm extended down, and your palms facing forward.
Simultaneously move your right arm up while moving your left arm down and lightly rotating your core, mimicking a swimming motion. Keep your arms straight throughout the movement.
Continue alternating arms in a smooth, controlled motion for the desired repetitions.
tips: Keep your core tight to maintain balance and stability.
Focus on keeping your movements smooth and fluid, avoiding any jerky motions.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you move your arms back and inhale as you return to the starting position.
results.description: Standing Swimmer is an intermediate multi-joint compound pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Core.

results.name: Standing Y Raise
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, with your arms extended forward, parallel to each other.
With slightly bent elbows, raise both arms diagonally overhead to form a "Y" shape.
Slowly lower your arms back to the starting position.
Repeat the movement for the desired repetitions
tips: Move slowly and with control to maximize muscle activation and avoid injury.
Breathe steadily: exhale as you raise your arms and inhale as you lower them.
Focus on keeping your arms in a diagonal line to form a "Y" shape and avoid any excessive swinging.
results.description: Standing Y Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing each other.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Pull the handles towards your face, bending your elbows and flaring them out to the sides until your hands are at face level.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull the handles towards your face and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Focus on using your upper back and shoulder muscles to perform the pull, avoiding excessive use of your arms.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Face Pull is an intermediate single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the handles with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with your arms extended straight in front of you and palms facing down.
Engage your core and lean back slightly, keeping your body straight from head to heels.
Keeping your arms straight, raise the handles upward until your arms are fully extended above your head, forming a straight line with your body.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep tension in the suspension trainer straps throughout the exercise.
Avoid letting your hips sag to maintain proper body alignment.
If you feel strain in your lower back, readjust your position and ensure your core is engaged.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Front Raise is an intermediate single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Core.

results.name: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row
instructions: Adjust the suspension trainer handles to about chest height. Stand facing the anchor point with your feet shoulder-width apart, holding the handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other), and lean back slightly with your arms extended.
Engage your upper back and pull your chest towards the handles by bending your elbows and driving them out to the sides, focusing on squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Continue pulling until your upper arms are parallel to the floor and your elbows are bent at a 90-degree angle.
Slowly extend your arms back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Breathe steadily: exhale as you pull your chest towards the handles and inhale as you extend your arms back.
Keep your core tight to maintain stability and prevent your hips from sagging.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them towards your ears.
results.description: Suspension Trainer With Grips Rear Delt Row is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a suspension trainer, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Biceps, Forearms.
